notes.decision: The isolated ϩⲉ on lines 13 and 15 (along with em-dashes on line 14) appear to be decorative borders framing the chapter heading — a common feature of Manichaean codex layout. Translated as em-dashes to preserve the framing function.

Re-analyzed against the tentative glossary reading 'is paired-with.' Here parsed as conjunctive ⲧⲁ- (1sg) + ⲧⲥⲉⲃⲟ ('teach,' verbal form of ⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching,' per terminology guide) + ⲑⲏⲛⲉ (2pl object suffix) = 'and I shall teach you (pl.).' The narrative context — Mani about to expound the cloud-mystery — strongly favors this reading. ⲥⲃⲟ as 'teach' is firmly established.

Translated 'break her forth / spread her forth' — uses ⲃⲁϣ 'scatter / break apart' (in glossary, tentative) with 3sg.f object suffix -ⲥ̄ referring back to ⲧⲕⲗⲟⲟⲗⲉ 'the cloud.' Captures the cosmic agents' act of dispatching the cloud.

Translated 'over against the likeness' — ⲟⲩⲃⲉ ('against, opposite, before,' standard Coptic) + ⲡⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness,' per terminology guide). Captures the spatial-correspondential register: the rising cloud stands as the visible counterpart against the heavenly likeness of the Virgin of Light.

Translated 'the sign' — likely ⲡ + ⲥⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ where ⲥⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ = ⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'sign, token' with prosthetic ⲥ-, or alternatively the verbal noun of ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ 'establish' substantivized. Either way, the cloud is identified as the visible sign of the Virgin of Light's gaze.

Translated as 'strike (them) / strike upon' throughout. The recurring verb ⲟⲁⲡ (lines 3, 6, 30) and reduplicated ⲟⲁⲙⲟⲙ (line 4) function in parallel with attested ⲧⲱⲙⲧ ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'reach upon' (line 8) and ⲧⲉⲍⲁϩ 'reach' (line 27, 29) as verbs of archonic violent contact with their targets. Etymology uncertain — possibly Lyc reflex of a striking-verb (cf. ⲱⲡ 'count, render judgment upon' under semantic shift). The two forms (ⲟⲁⲡ vs reduplicated ⲟⲁⲙⲟⲙ) may be morphological variants of the same root.

Parsed as habitual negative ⲙⲁⲩ-ⲣ̄-ⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲛ 'they do no good' (Greek ἀγαθόν, with regular Lyc. ⲫ for ⲑ) + ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'ever' (Lyc for ⲉⲛⲉϩ). Translation: 'they never do any good' = 'they are utterly unprofitable.' This explains why the angels strike them: the cloud-archons are inveterately destructive.

ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ from Greek φορεῖν 'wear (as garment)' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). With locative ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ/ⲙⲙⲁⲩ 'there' the construction means 'don themselves (in disguise) there.' The cloud-archons clothe themselves in a robber-disguise upon arriving at their target locale — matching the ⲗⲏⲥⲧⲏⲥ 'thief/robber' simile that follows.

Parsed as ⲡⲉⲧ- (relative) + ⲁⲩ-ⲟⲩⲱⲛ-ⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲧ-ⲁⲣⲁϩ '[which] they have opened the way upon (it).' The tree is one along their destructive route. Alternative parsing as 'on which they have set the path' yields the same sense. Confidence moderate due to lacuna and unusual idiom.

ⲭⲉⲥⲧ 'convey upward' (per accumulated vocabulary, normally salvific) here used cosmologically of the cloud being lifted up against the Virgin of Light — a hostile ascent (cf. accumulated entry ⲭⲉⲥⲧ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ ⲟⲩⲃⲉ 'rise up against'). The 3sg.f object suffix -ⲥ refers to ⲧⲕⲗⲟⲟⲗⲉ 'the cloud.'

Translated as 'the place' (Lyc. variant of ⲡⲙⲁ). Could alternatively read as 'the water' (Lyc. for ⲡⲙⲟⲟⲩ) which would fit the cloud-formation context naturally. Both readings yield coherent sense; 'the place' (the lower world from which the cloud rises) preferred for parallel with ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ 'the upper place.'

Translated as 'the form/likeness.' Likely Lyc. compound ⲥⲙ-ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'form-likeness' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ 'this manner/fashion' on ⲥⲙⲟⲧ + ⲉⲓⲛⲉ). Functions as identifying noun: 'the form is that of the thunders and lightnings.'
Translated as 'the lightnings.' Paired with ⲛⲓⲍⲣⲟⲩⲙⲡⲉ 'the thunders' (in glossary). Likely a Lycopolitan term for lightning — cf. tentative ⲙⲉⲕⲡⲉ 'lightning' in glossary. Etymology uncertain.

Two distinct cold-weather terms in the trio with ⲭⲁⲗⲁⲍⲁ 'hail' (Greek χάλαζα). ⲭⲓⲱⲛ = Greek χιών 'snow.' ⲭⲉϩ likely native Coptic ϫⲁϥ 'frost' or analogous term. Translated as 'frost / hail / snow' to preserve the threefold inventory of destructive precipitation.

Translated 'while my members' literally. The first-person possessive 'my' is striking — likely the perspective shifts here to the cosmic Living Soul / Cross of Light speaking, whose 'members' (= the light-particles dispersed through creation) are the targets struck by the archons. This shift commonly occurs in Manichaean cosmological discourse where the suffering Cross of Light speaks in first person.

Translated 'to reckon them.' Analyzed as ⲁ-ⲧ(ⲣⲉ-)ⲟⲩ-ⲟⲩⲱⲡ-ⲟⲩ 'to make them count' or causative-purpose construction on ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' (in glossary), with prosthetic ⲟⲩ- and Lyc. vowel-split ⲱ → ⲟ̄ⲁ. The same form recurs as ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲟ̄ⲁⲡⲟⲩ (l.12) and ⲥⲉⲟ̄ⲁⲡⲟⲩ (l.23) confirming 3pl object suffix on a reckoning-verb.

Translated as a doublet 'flight and dispersal' — ⲡⲱⲧ 'flee' (verbal noun) + ⲛ̄ⲥⲱⲣ 'and scattering' (cf. glossary ⲡⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲥ 'gatherer' inversely). The phrase opens by referencing topics from end of previous page.

Translated 'shall be raised up' — relative future on ϫⲓⲥⲉ 'raise, be high' with 3sg.f object. Same root underlies ⲡⲭⲥⲉ 'the Height' (in glossary). Note this is distinct from the soteriological ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise.'

Translated 'the gloom of wind.' ⲛⲟⲫⲟⲥ < Greek γνόφος/κνέφας 'gloom, gathering darkness.' The dark-wind/gloomy-wind is the first of three Virgin-of-Light signs catalogued in this chapter, paired with vehemence/harshness.
Translated 'gusts.' Lexeme uncertain; likely Lyc. plural for 'wind-gusts, blasts' paired with ⲛⲓⲧⲏⲩ 'winds.' Could alternatively be 'storms' or 'breezes.' Confidence moderate.
Translated 'they habitually make waves.' Habitual ϣⲁⲩ- + ⲣ̄- + ⲍⲁⲓⲙⲉ from ϩⲟⲉⲓⲙ/ⲍⲓⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'wave' (in glossary). The cloud-and-wind, descending into rivers and seas, agitates them.
Translated 'their ships.' Lyc. ⲝⲏⲩ likely = ϫⲏⲩ 'ships' (per glossary entry ⲛⲉⲭⲏⲩ for cosmic light-vessels). Fits the maritime sequence: rivers/seas → waves → ships → fish.

Translated 'one habitually finds her gathered.' ϣⲁⲕ-ⲟ̄ⲛⲧ-ⲥ as Lyc. habitual+verb+3sg.f, possibly from ϭⲛ̄ 'find.' ⲉⲥ-ⲥⲟ̄ⲏⲣ circumstantial 'while she is gathered/at rest.' The Virgin-sign is one of stillness and quiet.
Translated 'quietness.' Lexeme paired here twice with ⲟⲩⲍⲣⲁⲕ 'stillness' as a cosmic-quietude doublet. Likely related to ϭⲁⲙⲏ/ϫⲁⲙⲏ 'tranquility, calm.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'the cloud also which habitually departs upward.' Note that ⲭⲉⲥⲧ in glossary is 'depart upward / be raised up,' confirming the editor's restoration of ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' at the end of this line.

Tentatively translated 'an unutterable thing of them.' Analyzed as ⲛ̄ⲟⲩ- (indefinite art.) + ⲁⲧ- (privative) + ⲟⲩⲱ ('utter, declare') + ⲟⲩ (3pl) = 'an undeclared/unutterable (thing) of them.' Could alternatively be 'innumerable.' Confidence low.

Translated as 'they reckon them and receive them.' ⲥⲉⲟⲁⲡⲟⲩ from ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' (in glossary) with 3pl object; ⲛⲥⲉϣⲁⲡⲟⲩ from ϣⲱⲡ 'receive' with 3pl object. The cosmic-juridical register (counting + receiving) fits the angelic management of souls being processed through the transmigration cycle.
Standard Coptic idiom 'a stripping naked' (cf. accumulated ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ). The cosmic refinement is here described as a stripping-bare of the soul from its bodily/archonic integument.

Read as Lyc. variant of Sahidic ⲥⲱϫⲡ̄ 'leave behind, leave remaining.' The construction ϣⲁⲩⲥⲱⲭⲛ̄ ⲁⲡⲁⲍⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲟⲧⲟⲩ 'they habitually leave behind from out of their hand' fits the soul-residue motif. ⲭ for ϫ is regular Lyc.
Read as Lyc. reflex of ⲡⲱϩ/ⲧⲣⲉ-ⲡⲱϩ 'reach, attain' (causative or strong-form). The relative-future ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲛⲁⲧⲉⲍⲁϩ = 'in which they will reach.' Distinct from ⲧⲉϩⲟ 'to reach' in glossary.

Read tentatively as Lyc. ϫⲱⲱⲙⲉ/ⲱⲱⲙⲉ 'swallow' or related — fits the metempsychosis motif of the souls being absorbed into the begetting. Translation 'they swallow' supplies a tentative verb governing the surviving form. Confidence low.
Translated 'transfer/take them' from ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄ 'pass over, transfer' (Lyc.) — captures the angels' translation of the captive souls into their own midst, parallel to ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲙⲏⲧⲉ in next line.

ⲁⲁⲙⲱⲛ identified as Lyc. orthographic reduction of ⲇⲁⲓⲙⲱⲛ 'demons' (Greek δαίμων, in glossary). The cosmogonic act of casting the demons upward to the seven foundation-trenches outside the cosmos matches the standard Manichaean schema of expelling dark substance to the cosmic edge.

Parsed ⲁ-ⲟⲩ-ⲱⲱⲡⲉ 'unto a being/becoming of archons' — i.e., 'in the form of/disguised as archons.' ⲱⲱⲡⲉ = ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become' (cf. accumulated ⲱⲱⲡⲉ ⲉⲧⲉⲧⲛ̄ⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ). The angels are sent in archonic guise to police the archons' transgressions.

Obscure verbal form. Tentatively rendered 'watching over them' on contextual grounds — pairs with the restored ⲛⲟⲩⲛ̄ⲃⲁⲗ 'their eyes' and the upcoming 'until the hour in which' marker of vigilant watching. Possibly Lyc. reflex of ϫⲱϣⲧ̄ 'look upon, watch' (with ⲭ for ϫ) with feminine object suffix referring to a singular collective. Confidence low.

Read as Lyc. reflex of ⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'wipe out, dissolve, pour forth' (cf. accumulated entry); -ⲟⲩ is 3pl object suffix. The angels pour the refined souls forth from the upper place to be re-stationed in their original forms/icons — eschatological recapitulation.

Translated 'they swallow them' from ⲱⲙⲕ̄ 'swallow, devour' with 3pl object suffix. The archons swallow the bodies/souls in the begetting-cycle of flesh — the cosmic devouring of light-particles by archonic procreation.
Translated 'drawn back' per accumulated vocabulary entry ⲥⲱⲝⲧ̄ ⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'draw back / regress'. The subjects appear to be the archons, who have retreated behind from the action of the cosmic refinement.
Read ⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ here as a verbal use ('fall back, retreat to') rather than the standard adverbial 'behind'; the conjunctive future ⲉⲩϣⲁⲛ- requires a verb. Confidence moderate.

Tentatively translated 'snatchings-forth.' The ⲱⲗ-ⲁⲃⲁⲗ family covers 'carry/lift forth'; cf. accumulated ⲁⲗⲱⲭϩ̅ 'extract, snatch out' and ⲟ̄ⲁⲗⲟ̄ⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'draw out, lift forth.' The plural noun would name characteristic archonic operations of seizing light from souls. Confidence low; the lexeme is unattested in our corpus.

Read as Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'fall, sink' with directional ⲁⲣⲁⲩ 'upon them.' The agent ('they fall upon them') is taken as continuing from the archonic subject of the previous clause; alternatively the angels of line 10 may be the assailants. Translation 'fall upon them' fits the punitive cosmological flow culminating in the archons' imprisonment.

Translated 'prison' here rather than 'Zone/Girdle.' The accumulated glossary lists ⲧϩⲱⲛⲏ as 'prison/fastness (tentative)' or possibly = ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ 'the cosmic Zone.' The immediate context (archons cast into a structure 'which is outside,' guarded by angels under the Virgin of Light's authority) decisively favors the prison-of-archons reading consistent with Manichaean cosmography of the bound dark powers in the zodiacal Zone.

Restored as ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ qualitative 'refines, smelts, filters' (cf. ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄/ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ in metallurgical sense). The cosmic prison/Zone is described as the locus where the captive Life is refined upward through the celestial vessels — standard Manichaean cosmography.

Tentatively read as Lycopolitan variant of ⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'manner, fashion' (cf. ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ in glossary). With ⲛ̄- 'of' it would yield 'the manner of [exposition/narration] of all the apocalypses.' Lexeme uncertain; could alternatively be an unidentified noun.

Parsed as ⲛⲙ̄- ('and/with') + ⲡⲉⲧ-ϩⲏⲧ ('that-which-is-within' or 'the foremost') + ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ ('all'). Translated 'with all that is within' — the inward/hidden contents of the apostle's revelation that have been disclosed to the disciples.
